answers.stem_only: Use an FSx for Lustre scratch file system linked to the S3 bucket (data repository association): it lazy-loads input from S3, gives very high throughput, and is the cheapest Lustre type because data is not replicated; the job tolerates server loss by re-reading from S3. Write results back to S3 with an export (data repository export task or auto-export) before the file system is deleted. No backups and no persistent deployment are needed.

Use Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket. The file system imports only metadata at creation and lazy-loads file contents on first access, so training can start at once and each job pulls only the part of the dataset it reads; it gives a shared high-throughput POSIX file system for the GPU cluster. Export the trained models back to the bucket (export task or auto-export). No bulk copy with DataSync and no per-instance downloads.

Migrate to Amazon FSx for OpenZFS: it is a managed ZFS file system accessed over NFS, so Linux applications need no code change, and it supports point-in-time snapshots and writable clone volumes created from a snapshot, which keeps the test teams' snapshot-to-clone workflow (automated through the FSx API or CLI).
